title: Outlook for Mac: Purview DLP wait-on-send support
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap plan and distinguishes documented Windows controls from unpublished Mac wait-on-send details. Minor corrections should acknowledge the published general DLP licensing, complete the two portal paths, and disclose conflicting Microsoft guidance about Mac policy tips.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Mac wait-on-send default and what happens on arrival are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac Purview DLP wait on send default timeout licensing price administrator settings. Read roadmap, Mac/mobile policy-tip reference, new Outlook reference and Set-OrganizationConfig; defaults found concern Windows, not Mac.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because a requirement specific to Outlook for Mac wait on send is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac Purview DLP wait on send default timeout licensing price administrator settings. Read Purview service description and Mac/mobile, classic and new Outlook references; general Exchange DLP entitlements are published, but no Mac wait-on-send-specific requirement.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included under the standard's product-level licensing rule. Add to licensing.notes and Cost and licensing: 'Exchange Online DLP requires an eligible licence, such as Microsoft 365 E3 or E5; Microsoft has not published a requirement specific to Mac wait on send.' Use the already cited Microsoft Purview service description. Retain the caveat against assuming Windows oversharing requirements apply to Mac.

claims.claim: Microsoft has published no price specific to Mac wait on send.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac Purview DLP wait on send default timeout licensing price administrator settings; Outlook Mac wait on send oversharing dialog Exchange DLP roles licensing metered. Read Purview service description and Mac/mobile, classic and new Outlook references.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe Mac wait-on-send behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac Purview DLP wait on send default timeout licensing price administrator settings; DLPWaitOnSendEnabled DLPWaitOnSendTimeout admin center UI Mac registry group policy. Read Mac/mobile, classic and new Outlook policy-tip references and oversharing setup.

claims.claim: No admin-centre path for the Exchange wait-on-send parameters is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled DLPWaitOnSendTimeout admin center UI Mac registry group policy. Read Set-OrganizationConfig, new Outlook, Mac/mobile and classic Outlook references and oversharing setup; found PowerShell for Windows but no Exchange parameter UI or Mac switch.

claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -DLPWaitOnSendEnabled $true -DLPWaitOnSendTimeout <seconds> configures the Exchange organisation wait-on-send settings.
claims.quote: Use the Set-OrganizationConfig cmdlet to configure various settings of an Exchange organization. [-DLPWaitOnSendEnabled <Boolean>] [-DLPWaitOnSendTimeout <Int16>]

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The Exchange wait-on-send parameters are documented for new Outlook for Windows but not confirmed for Mac.
claims.quote: Searched: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled DLPWaitOnSendTimeout admin center UI Mac registry group policy. Read Set-OrganizationConfig and new Outlook and Mac/mobile references; Windows explicitly names these parameters, while no passage ties them to Mac.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management reaches the management area for the Mac policy-tips setting.
claims.quote: You can access this policy under Customization and Policy Management.
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Customization > Policy Management > Create > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook > Enabled'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy alongside the current reference for the creation steps. The existing path is correct but stops at the policy list.

claims.claim: An API for the Microsoft 365 Apps policy-tips policy is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention DLP policy tips Outlook cloud policy Microsoft Graph API PowerShell; Cloud Policy service Microsoft 365 Apps API automation Graph create policy configuration. Read Mac/mobile reference and Cloud Policy overview; no policy-setting API found.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook controls policy-tip UI in Outlook for Mac.
claims.quote: To enable Policy Tip UI to appear in Outlook for Android, iOS, and macOS, you must enable the policy listed in the following section in the Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center.
claims.fix: Add to the control note: 'The platform reference documents Mac policy tips, although Resolve issues that affect DLP policy tips still says policy tips are not supported for Outlook for Mac iOS clients.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/troubleshoot/microsoft-365/purview/data-loss-prevention/data-loss-prevention-policy-tips#client-doesn't-support-mailtips for that conflicting statement; retain the platform reference as the basis for the control.

claims.claim: The policy can target individuals.
claims.quote: You can target policies to individuals or groups

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The policy can target groups for testing and deployment.
claims.quote: You can target policies to individuals or groups, so you can test and deploy policy tip UI as needed through your organization.

claims.claim: Policy-tip UI is off by default in Outlook for Android, iOS and macOS until an admin enables the policy.
claims.quote: Policy Tip UI is turned off by default in Outlook for Android, iOS, and macOS to allow for administrators to test and perform user training prior to deployment.

claims.claim: The documented policy governs policy-tip visibility rather than configuring wait on send.
claims.quote: Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook | (default) Disabled policy tips aren't shown Enabled policy tips are shown

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies reaches the policies used for oversharing dialog configuration.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom (Categories) > Custom (Regulations) > Full directory (Admin units) > Exchange email > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > User notifications > Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only)'. State in the note that User notifications must be On. The existing path is correct but stops at the policies list.

claims.claim: The abbreviated New-DlpComplianceRule call with Owner notifications, Dialog display, a label condition and trusted-domain exceptions configures a warn pop-up rule.
claims.quote: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <DLP Rule Name> -Policy <DLP Policy Name> -NotifyUser Owner -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption "Dialog" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation

claims.claim: The full warn-rule command reproduces Learn's sensitivity-label condition structure and recipient-domain exception.
claims.quote: -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @(@{operator = "And"; groups = @(@{operator="Or";name="Default";labels=@(@{name=<Label GUID>;type="Sensitivity"})})}) -ExceptIfRecipientDomainIs @("contoso.com","microsoft.com")

claims.where: Governance controls: Full warn-rule example introduction
claims.claim: Label GUID identifies the sensitivity label in the documented condition.
claims.quote: Configures one or more sensitivity label conditions. This sample includes one. At least one label is mandatory. labels=@(@{name=<Label GUID>;type="Sensitivity"})

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls: Full warn-rule example introduction
claims.claim: ExceptIfRecipientDomainIs supplies trusted recipient domains.
claims.quote: -ExceptIfRecipientDomainIs | List of trusted domains.

claims.claim: The documented oversharing dialog option is described for Outlook for Microsoft 365, without confirmation for Mac.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac wait on send oversharing dialog Exchange DLP roles licensing metered. Read oversharing setup and Mac/mobile, classic and new Outlook references; the Mac/mobile oversharing section names Android and iOS, not macOS.

claims.claim: Outlook for Microsoft 365 wait on send is configured with the dlpwaitonsendtimeout registry key.
claims.quote: you can optionally enable the Wait on send dialog feature using the dlpwaitonsendtimeout Registry key (DWORD value).

claims.claim: Specify wait time to evaluate sensitive content is the documented Group Policy setting for classic Outlook wait on send.
claims.quote: You can set this RegKey via group policy, Specify wait time to evaluate sensitive content, script, or other mechanism for configuring registry keys.

claims.claim: The Mac/mobile reference's wait-on-send section names Android and iOS, not macOS, as not yet supporting wait on send.
claims.quote: Outlook for Android and iOS doesn't yet support DLP Wait-to-Send

claims.claim: In classic Outlook, an unconfigured wait-on-send setting sends the email immediately.
claims.quote: When dlpwaitonsendtimeout isn't configured, the message isn't checked before the user sends it. The email message is sent immediately once Send is clicked.

claims.claim: In that classic Outlook configuration, DLP evaluation and policy actions occur after sending.
claims.quote: The email message is sent immediately once Send is clicked. The DLP data classification service evaluates the message and apply the actions defined in the DLP policy.

claims.claim: Classic Outlook allows configured timeout values from 0 to 9999 seconds.
claims.quote: The T value range is 0 to 9999 seconds.

claims.claim: Classic Outlook offers Send anyway when evaluation exceeds the configured timeout in that range.
claims.quote: If the policy evaluation doesn't complete in the specified time a Send anyway button appears allowing the user to bypass the presend check.

claims.claim: Classic Outlook timeout values above 9999 are replaced with 10000.
claims.quote: If the T value is greater than 9999, it's replaced with 10000

claims.claim: That classic Outlook configuration holds the message until evaluation finishes without a Send anyway override.
claims.quote: the Send Anyway button doesn't appear. This holds the message until the policy evaluation completes and doesn't provide the user with an override option.

claims.claim: In new Outlook for Windows, timeout 0 shows Send Anyway immediately.
claims.quote: When DLPWaitOnSendTimeout = 0, user will immediately see "Send Anyway" in the infobar of mail.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: How the Mac wait-on-send timeout is configured is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled DLPWaitOnSendTimeout admin center UI Mac registry group policy; Outlook Mac Purview DLP wait on send default timeout licensing price administrator settings. Read Mac/mobile, classic and new Outlook references, Set-OrganizationConfig and oversharing setup.

claims.claim: Matching DLP block rules block the message regardless of the Policy tips configuration.
claims.quote: If the block rules defined in the DLP policy are met, the message will be blocked regardless of how Policy tips is configured.

claims.claim: Classic Outlook evaluation duration varies with internet speed, content length and the number of policies.
claims.quote: The duration for completing the evaluation can vary depending on factors such as internet speed, content length, and the number of policies defined.

claims.claim: Some classic Outlook users encounter evaluation messages more frequently than others.
claims.quote: Some users may encounter policy evaluation messages more frequently than others, depending on the policies that are deployed on their mailbox.
